default.title: Go keeps compile times short
default.content: Go compiles large command-line tools in seconds, which suits fast iteration. Rust builds of similar size often take minutes in release mode.

default.title: Rust prevents data races at compile time
default.content: Rust's ownership rules reject data races before the program runs. Go relies on a race detector that only finds races during tests.

default.title: Binary size comparison
default.content: A small Go tool produced a 4 MB binary while the Rust version was 1.5 MB after stripping. Both start in under 10 milliseconds.

default.title: Hiring and learning curve
default.content: Developers reported reaching productivity in Go in about two weeks and in Rust in about two months.

default.title: Ecosystem for CLI parsing
default.content: Both ecosystems offer mature argument-parsing libraries. Rust's clap and Go's cobra are each used by thousands of tools.
